text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition Kisumu rural parliament member Anyang' Nyong'o confirms widespread speculation by announcing that he will soon quit main opposition FORD-Kenya party for moribund Social Democratic Party.
- President Daniel arap Moi said the government would deal firmly with criminals to ensure law and order in the country.

- At least a dozen Ugandan ministers could face eviction from their residences in the capital Kampala as a result of a government directive that they must start paying rent at market rates. The rents are at around $1,500 while their housing allowance is pegged at $500.
- A regional delegation of East African foreign ministers finally visited Burundi after an apparent change of heart by the military regime of Major Pierre Buyoya in Bujumbura.
- Roman Catholic Church condemns leaders who manipulated people by exploiting their ethnic background in order to consolidate their hold on political power and wealth.
- "No mercy for terror thugs", President Moi says in confirming his government will deal firmly and mercilessly with criminals who have terrorised Kenyans in recent weeks.
- President Moi says electoral commission is absolutely independent and there is no interference in its acitivities by the Kenyan government.

- Minister in charge of internal security Jackson Kalweo says the government has launched independent investigations to establish the involvement of some security personnel in apparent organised crime in Nairobi and its environs.
